audit.why: 51.65% over 788 games. A genuine poke war: the 2-3 gate-Q window is Jayce's, the middle is a stalemate because Teemo kites the only thing that kills him, and shrooms take the side lane from two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every stage on the chart disagrees with its own caption except the last. whys[0] says 'we trade orbs and farm even' under a Jayce level 1; whys[1] says 'this is my window' under a Skill level 2; whys[2] says 'the early favor is mine' under a Teemo level 3; whys[3] says 'the poke war neutralizes' under a Teemo 4-5; whys[4] says 'neither side pulls clearly ahead' under a Jayce level 6; whys[5] says 'a coinflip with no owner' under a Teemo first item.
audit.why: Six of seven stages are sided against their own text, and the two 7/10 ratings sit on the stages the text calls even. Packet reference chart Skill|Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Skill|Skill|Teemo is precisely what the captions argue.
audit.corrected: Sides re-set to Skill, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Skill, Skill, Teemo.

audit.why: The decisive interaction is already stated and stated well: Blinding Dart blinds, so it stops autos and on-hit but cannot touch Shock Blast, which is a skillshot. The page leads with it and repeats it in wants.you[0]. The one thing worth adding is that the blind also blanks the Mercury Cannon swap's armor/MR first hit and every Hyper Charge shot, since both are attacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells you to commit 'if his cooldowns are down' without a single number.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank and Move Quick is a flat 14s — neither scales, so the windows never get shorter. Noxious Trap is effectively off cooldown at 0.25s between throws once he has mushrooms stored.

edits.before: This is a poke war, not a takeover, and it stays even because he can kite the one thing that actually kills him. My burst needs me in Hammer form: Cannon-Q to land it, swap to shred his armor/MR on the first hit, then Hammer Q-W-E. But the instant I am in melee range his move speed and E-poison let him walk away, and that is when he holds Blinding Dart for my swap-auto. Keep poking with gate-Q from max range where he cannot trade back, and only commit the all-in if he mispositions against a wall or his cooldowns are down. At 6 I get nothing new, since my R is the swap I already had, while his R starts seeding shrooms, so the window is quietly tilting toward him.

notes: The prose here is already strong — the blind-does-not-stop-skillshots point is well made. The problem is purely the level chart: six of seven stages were sided against their own captions, with 7/10 ratings sitting on stages the text calls even. Blinding Dart and Move Quick have FLAT cooldowns (7s and 14s at every rank), so unlike most matchups the windows never shorten. The kit file gives Noxious Trap a 'knockup' derived flag; Riot's own description says it slows and damages over time, with no displacement, so I treated the flag as a tooltip-parsing misfire and put nothing about it on the page.
